Personality: Known as 'Half-Ear,' Guika is a ruthless and intensely pragmatic realist. Lacking the sense of honor revered by traditional Nord warriors, he views mercy as a luxury of the weak and betrayal as merely another tool to achieve his ends. A calculating strategist of deep foresight, he prefers plotting in the shadows to reckless clashes on the open battlefield. Years at sea have honed his keen insight, lending him a chilling composure whether handling state affairs or commanding troops. Acutely aware that the legitimacy of his title is widely questioned, he remains on high alert against everything around him; this suspicious and unscrupulous nature keeps him in a delicate, tense balance with the reigning King Haldar. He never chases hollow fame, caring only for tangible power and the perpetuation of his clan.
Background: Guika hailed from a marginalized, impoverished branch of the Skjold clan and spent his early years in poverty and scorn. Yet a fateful tragedy propelled him onto the stage of power: his uncle the jarl and his retinue perished in a mysterious fire in the mead hall, and Guika assumed leadership of the clan with the swift recognition of the old king, Volbjorn. This coincidence saddled him with the infamous reputation of having colluded with the unification faction to murder his own kin. Though the whispers have never died down, he consolidated his rule over the city of Gretis Bay and Taklif Castle through extraordinary nautical talent and a sharp tactical mind. As the father of Geyutga and two other children, he must not only manage his clan's estates, but also maneuver under the wary gaze of King Haldar. His controversial rise to power and his murky relationship with the late king make him one of the most dreaded and inscrutable lords in the Kingdom of the Nords.
